← Back to campus

A campus built from observation.

64 photo galleries, street-level views, architecture sources and elevation references used to guide the recreation. Photographs remain at their original sources; they are visual references, not copied game textures. Modelled façades and many dimensions remain approximations.

VILLAGE ARCHITECTURE

UNSW Village · Clare / Architectus gallery

Eight-storey thin-plan wings with lower boundary volumes, pale horizontal bands, deep balcony openings, yellow accents and communal courtyards. The model partitions the real OSM footprint; all new massing heights are reconstructed estimates.

UNSW Village · screened balcony detail

Closely spaced warm horizontal slats, grey metal frames and recessed glazing. Screens are rebuilt as geometry, not copied photographs.

UNSW Village · tall entry and lower end volume

Double-height entry, concrete frame, dark panelled tower and yellow wall. The architect confirms eight-storey main wings; exact floor-to-floor dimensions remain uncertain.

UNSW Village · architect ground plan

Courtyard openings and the east-west circulation spine. Four retained public OSM footways locate through-passages in the model; their extra width and overhead clearances are reconstructed.

INTERNATIONAL EXTERIOR

International House · official exterior

Light mixed brickwork, pale upper cladding, small horizontal upper windows and a deep dark roof fascia. Two visible exterior rows and a 7.8 m reconstruction are photo-led estimates; the retained map tag says three levels.

Timber picnic furniture, overhead shade structure and lush planted edges. Garden furniture is reconstructed; the model does not copy people or photo textures.

SHALOM EXTERIOR

Shalom · official accommodation exterior

Three visible room rows, tall narrow balcony doors, projecting balconies with dark vertical balusters and a deep roof edge. The college confirms first- and second-floor balconies. The source banner has a purple tint; colours are approximate. The 12 m mapped overall height is retained despite its conflicting four-level tag.

POSTGRADUATE EXTERIOR

New College Postgraduate Village · official street exterior

Large blue-glass screen, pale horizontal frames, blue-grey tower panels and a lower ochre side wing. The college describes seven floors; OSM tags eight levels. The reconstructed height split and facade spacing remain estimates.

NIDA UPPER

NIDA · Graduate School exterior

Upper metal-clad forms and glazed end above the original foyer roof. Actual OSM parts 609912635 / 638 have height=19 and min_height=12; part 609912640 is the D-shaped 17 m theatre shell. Those outlines replace the earlier round approximation; facade pitch and panel detailing remain reconstructed.

Open source ↗View photograph ↗
NIDA ARCHITECT

NIDA · original architect gallery

Hassell with Peter Armstrong Architecture: an eleven-metre curtain glass wall, skillion roof and louvred Parade Theatre. The 11 m dimension describes the curtain wall, separately from the retained 17 / 19 m OSM building-part height tags. The D-shaped theatre outline is mapped; roof pitch remains estimated.

Open source ↗
NIDA ENTRANCE

NIDA · official Anzac Parade exterior

Tall fine-framed glazing, a broad pale roof soffit, glass entrance box, dark theatre sign and ochre brick wing. Upper volumes now use actual mapped parts, but exact perforated artwork, roof pitch and interior structure remain incomplete.

NIDA DRUM

NIDA · louvred theatre drum

Patrick Bingham-Hall photograph: cylindrical auditorium wrapped in closely spaced pale horizontal louvres, dark structural posts and a roof opening. Image inspected at its source; no copied texture.

COLLEGES JOURNAL

Kensington Colleges · Bates Smart project journal

Printed pp. 180–183 / PDF pp. 92–93: five- and six-storey volumes step up the terrain. Courtyard faces have faceted glazed brickwork, balconies and narrow windows; outer faces use a three-shade clinker brick blend. Photographs inspected, not redistributed.
